why: Review of the 46 open-reader problems map-1 could not map: 25 had a matching code whose wording was narrower than its mechanism (a non-English restriction, a structural-only constraint list, a clause lost in the refinement split), and the harness's own field markers were being read as format breaches. Genuine gaps (fabricated missing input, response not addressing the request) are left for the next generation round.

amendments.name: linguistic_declension_and_grammatical_inflection_error
amendments.reason: the mechanism is not specific to non-English text; 5 English agreement errors ('an flame', 'My aim do not set') in map-1 were left unmapped because the name and definition said non-English

amendments.name: grammatical_agreement_or_inflection_error
amendments.before: During non-English text composition or translation work, the agent generates grammatically incorrect case inflection or modifier-noun agreement errors.
amendments.after: While composing or translating text in any language, the agent produces a grammatical agreement or inflection error: article–noun or modifier–noun agreement, subject–verb agreement, case, number or tense inflection.
amendments.reason: drop the non-English restriction; same mechanism in English

amendments.name: grammatical_agreement_or_inflection_error
amendments.before: Use when an agent makes a grammatical, case, or inflection error while composing text in a target language.
amendments.after: Use when a phrase the agent wrote is ungrammatical because of agreement, case, number or tense inflection, in any language, including when the error was made to satisfy another constraint (word length, letter counts).
amendments.reason: cover the English instances and the constraint-driven ones

amendments.name: grammatical_agreement_or_inflection_error
amendments.before: Do not use for structural, structural envelope, or layout failures.
amendments.after: Do not use for structural or layout failures, nor for text that is incoherent as a whole rather than grammatically wrong in a phrase.
amendments.reason: keep the boundary to the conformance code and to incoherence (uncoded)

amendments.name: output_conformance_and_structural_constraint_violation
amendments.before: The agent produces output that breaches explicit structural, length, envelope, or formatting rules, such as paragraph/sentence counts, JSON formatting requirements, outer quote wrappers, or required section content.
amendments.after: The agent produces output that breaches an explicit constraint the prompt places on the output itself: structural, length, envelope or formatting rules (paragraph/sentence counts, JSON, outer quote wrappers, required sections), lexical or character-level rules (required or forbidden words, letters, punctuation marks, letter patterns), or additions the prompt did not ask for (trailing filler, an unrequested closing phrase).
amendments.reason: map-1 left 6 constraint breaches unmapped (missing consonant cluster, missing exclamation mark, unbalanced brackets, unrequested filler) because the definition enumerated structural kinds only

amendments.name: output_conformance_and_structural_constraint_violation
amendments.before: Use when an output payload fails edge-conformance requirements (e.g. producing plain text instead of JSON, omitting required code blocks, failing minimum word/sentence counts, or providing incorrect paragraph numbers).
amendments.after: Use when the output fails a rule the prompt states about the output's form or wording: wrong format or envelope, wrong counts, a required or forbidden word or character present or absent, unbalanced wrappers, or content appended that no rule asked for.

amendments.name: output_conformance_and_structural_constraint_violation
amendments.before: Do not use when the error occurs inside internal reasoning calculations without manifesting as an unfulfilled output requirement.
amendments.after: Do not use when the output is well-formed but does not address the request's content, nor for errors inside reasoning that never reach the output, nor for verbatim-repetition failures, which have their own codes. The `[[ ## field ## ]]` markers around output fields and a `reasoning` field are the execution harness's own output format, declared in the instructions section and needed to parse the output; using them instead of a plainer layout described in the instruction text is not a failure of any kind.
amendments.reason: content adequacy is not a conformance breach; keep it visibly outside; 35 open-reader problems mapped here were the harness's own field markers

amendments.name: whitespace_and_microformatting_alteration_during_string_processing
amendments.before: In the middle of performing verbatim text processing or formatting work, the agent alters micro-formatting elements such as replacing double spaces with single spaces.
amendments.after: While transforming or reproducing a string (reversing, re-casing, re-spacing, copying), the agent alters character-level detail that the task requires kept: whitespace, punctuation placement, or other micro-formatting.
amendments.reason: 2 punctuation-placement errors during sentence reversal were left unmapped because the definition named whitespace only

amendments.name: whitespace_and_microformatting_alteration_during_string_processing
amendments.before: Use when string processing alters whitespace formatting (e.g., spacing after punctuation) within a string during verbatim handling steps.
amendments.after: Use when string processing changes spacing, punctuation position or similar character-level detail within the string being processed.

amendments.name: verbatim_repetition_text_modification
amendments.before: The model attempts to repeat the text but alters its surface representation through casing changes, symbol substitutions, formatting alterations, or language translation.
amendments.after: The model attempts to repeat the text but alters it: casing changes, symbol substitutions, formatting alterations, translation, or text included that is not part of the target, such as the instruction sentence copied into the repetition.
amendments.reason: the refinement edit added 'incorrectly including meta-instruction text' and the split lost it; 1 such instance was left unmapped in map-1

amendments.name: verbatim_repetition_text_modification
amendments.before: Use when the repeated text content is provided but deviates from verbatim matching due to formatting, character substitution, or translation.
amendments.after: Use when the repeated text is present but deviates from verbatim: formatting, character substitution, translation, or extra text mixed into the repeated block.
